Reliably predicting temporal development of complex systems proves essential across
multiple scientific domains. This profound interest encounters obstacles from
representation challenges: frequently, governing equations describing underlying phenomena of the
system under examination remain inaccessible or, when available, their resolution
demands computational duration incompatible with prediction timeline
requirements. Unsurprisingly, approximating elaborate structures using generic
functional formats and informing them ex-nihilo from existing data has
emerged as standard methodology during the machine intelligence era, as demonstrated by
countless successful instances relying on deep neural architectures. Nevertheless,
transferability of learned models, safety margins and observational influence are
frequently neglected or explored primarily by depending on prior understanding of the
underlying mechanics. We address these obstacles from an alternative perspective, by adopting a
progressive instruction strategy. In progressive curriculum learning, the collection is organized
such that the preparation procedure begins from elementary samples toward increasingly sophisticated
ones to promote optimization and transfer. The concept has been
developed and fruitfully implemented in robotics and task management. Here, we
employ this concept for acquiring knowledge of intricate dynamical behaviors in a
methodical fashion. Initially, leveraging insights from ergodic theory, we evaluate
the volume of measurements sufficient for a-priori ensuring a faithful approximation of the target dynamics under study.
lexical_diversity_up_more.coling::4b504a77-e4f6-447f-996a-b39d54b5: (CNN) The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels vowed not to back down on Sunday as a top Saudi military official claimed weeks of airstrikes had significantly weakened the Shiite group. "Our fighters will not evacuate from the main cities or the government institutions," rebel commander Abdul-Malik al-Houthi said in a televised address. "Anyone who thinks we will surrender is dreaming." His comments came after more than three weeks of Saudi-led coalition bombings aimed at pushing back the Houthis, who surged into the capital of Sanaa in January and ousted President Abdu Rabu Monsour Hadi from power. Hadi still claims he's Yemen's legitimate ruler and is working with the Saudis and other allies to return to his country. Since mid-March, more than 700 people have been killed in violence that shows no sign of slowing, according to figures from the World Health Organization. The Houthis say they have the support of the country's population behind them. "It's the right of the Yemeni people to stand against the attacks in all possible means as long as the bombardment continues," Al-Houthi stated Sunday. "After our citizens move and react against the assaults and killing of children and women, we do not want to hear any voices and cries." But there are signs of some fracturing among forces loyal to former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh, many of whom have fought alongside the insurgents. Gen. AbdulRahman AlHalili, who leads more than 10,000 troops, has now allied himself with Hadi, military sources announced Sunday. Meanwhile, Saudi Brig. Gen. Ahmed Asiri reported Sunday that airstrikes had decimated the Houthis' central command by targeting their communications. The rebels, he noted, are now holding a defensive stance in besieged areas. Since it began the campaign known as Operation Decisive Storm on March 26, the Saudi-led coalition has launched 2,300 strikes, Asiri mentioned. After hours at sea, chaos and desperation in Yemeni city. CNN's Don Melvin and Christine Theodorou contributed to this story. The situation remains fluid as international observers monitor developments across multiple regions experiencing conflict and ongoing hostilities throughout various territories.
lexical_diversity_up_more.coling::f4961832-eeb4-41fc-8a64-82c30107: Let me preface this by stating that I genuinely appreciate Cowboy Bebop. The animation plus designs prove sublime, the soundtrack remains fantastic, the action sequences appear great, and when all three combine the program can occasionally become a jaw-dropping audiovisual masterpiece, particularly in the breathtaking finale. However, there exist so many problems with it that I cannot in good faith call it a "triumph" or proclaim it to be among the finest of the medium as anything other than an introductory offering. I'll start off with the cast, which is where numerous concerns lie. I'll admit, Spike and Jet constitute excellent protagonists, but they represent only 25 of the entire Bebop Crew. Ein's introduction as a "data dog" or otherwise hyperintelligent canine goes nowhere and he spends the remainder of the show just being the crew's pet. Faye exhibits numerous worst characteristics that can be written about a female personality; she's bossy, greedy, obsessed with her own beauty, needs to either be rescued or proves a hinderance to the group more often than an asset, she frequently wears revealing clothing for the sole purpose of fanservice. Ed is hit or miss, and walks the line separating endearing and annoying, but hardly receives much development beyond her introductory installment. The main villain Vicious is especially bad. He has very little personality and motivation aside from a desire for additional power, and even though the show goes somewhat into his backstory it never establishes rationale. At the conclusion of the narrative, Vicious is little more than an evil guy in a black coat with enough fighting skill that it makes Spike struggle to land a bullet in him, aside from the obvious fact that Vicious becomes a representation of the syndicate Spike ran away from. As a result the five episodes that involve him (Sympathy for the Devil, Jupiter Jazz pts 12, and Real Folk Blues pts 12) don't leave me feeling as if they are as spectacular as the show wants me to feel like they remain. Aside from that, the quality of the installments varies dramatically. For an episodic production that only has approximately five chapters building an overall story, that's saying a lot. Sure, there exist fantastic entries such as Waltz for Venus and Ganymede Elegy, but there are also fairly ho hum segments such as Bohemian Rhapsody, Speak Like a Child, and Boogie Woogie Feng Shui.
